intelligence.ai_view: For builder seats — exact hooks at tip b276ba0d (files byte-identical to 80dab8d3 for all three tools files). WRITER: tools/smart_note_v2.py publish_classic() stamps final_capture before the capture write: add published_via='publish-note', door_version, and door_receipt = sha256(canonical_json(capture_without_receipt) || page_hash || prev_content_hash), where prev_content_hash is the content_hash of the last entry in the registry entries array read inside the same registry_transaction (genesis prev = 64 zero hex chars). register_classic() stores door_receipt on the entry. CHECKER: tools/check_door_obligation.py — (a) CaptureIndex (L256) must additionally index by capture filename stem, top-level file/intelligent_block_id, and registry capture_file, because classic captures carry neither projection_path nor intelligent_block_id inside intelligence and for_page() (L287) therefore misses every classic capture today, manufacturing false NO_CAPTURE/CONFLICT verdicts (the SN-4203..4207 class); (b) NO_CAPTURE must be checked whenever an entry's capture_file is set, not only nested inside NO_ENTRY (check_pages L305); (c) verify registry corpus_manifest_hash by recomputation every run — the writer re-stamps it inside registry_transaction on every publish, so a stale manifest is already proof of an out-of-door registry edit, and today the checker never looks; (d) verify the receipt chain across all door-stamped entries in stored order; legacy entries predate the chain and are grandfathered by an explicit ratchet list, and fixer entries stay permanently marked provenance.ingestion='canonical-reconstruction' and chain-exempt — visible forever as non-door. GATE: .github/workflows/door-obligation.yml must report on every PR (delta exits 0 fast when no note paths are touched) so it can be made a REQUIRED status check in ruleset without pending-forever PRs; bypass actors are removed for BRAIN/05-MEMORY/**, .naya/capture/**, .naya/memory/** so the pull_request rule binds automated identities on note paths too. BACKSTOP: tools/regenerate_brain_index.py excludes pages with no verified registry entry instead of absorbing them (its floors-only ratchet currently legitimizes bare pages); post-merge-guardian auto-reverts the narrow door-defect class instead of only preparing a revert PR. SCOPE DECISION, named not smoothed: the parallel BRAIN/05-MEMORY/NAYA-NOTES corpus (1,317 NN-*.md at tip) sits outside the door obligation entirely; this design does not silently absorb it — the law must either bring NN under the same door or exempt it by a filed note, and until that ruling the sealed perimeter is the SN corpus exactly.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine a library where every new book must be stamped at the front desk, and the librarian writes its name in a big book, each name tied to the one before it with a knot. If someone sneaks a book onto a shelf without the stamp, the knot pattern breaks and the librarian spots it right away — and the shelf only shows books whose knots are right, so the sneaky book might as well not be there. This plan makes the library work like that, so everybody just uses the front desk.
intelligence.essence: Thirty-two registry cures proved the same fact: filing lanes file Smart Notes around the publish-note door because nothing at the writer side stops them — the registry is a plain JSON file anyone with repo write can edit, every hash is a public formula, and no landing check is required by any ruleset. The Sealed Door design closes the bypass in three layers: (1) a receipt chain minted only inside the door, each entry chained to the previous entry's content hash, so a valid receipt can only be produced by running the door against the live registry; (2) the door-obligation checker completed — it learns to see classic captures, verifies the corpus manifest and the chain on every run; (3) a required landing gate (door-obligation as a required check, bypass actors narrowed for note paths) plus a consumer backstop, so any bypass that still lands is invisible downstream and auto-reverted. Winner of a five-option scorecard at 7.5/10. No option scores higher, and the design says why: two facts sit outside any design's reach — main requires no status check today (one settings change, Shawn's hand), and every seat shares one GitHub identity, so authorship can never be proven inside the repo (SN-0111: a seal proves consistency, not authorship). The graduation test is a red-team pass over all four known bypass routes plus three consecutive filing batches with zero band and zero cures; when it passes, the cure lane retires and P-152 graduates.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, the team keeps finding books in the library that never went past the front desk, and they have cleaned that up thirty-two times. This plan fixes the cause instead of the mess: the front desk ties every new entry to the last one with a thread nobody can fake without going through the desk itself, the inspector checks the thread every visit, the door check becomes required rather than optional, and the shelves only display properly tied books. After that, sneaking a book in gains you nothing — it never reaches a reader — so nobody bothers, and the cleaning-up job can finally end.
intelligence.human_view: Right now the Smart Note library has a front door — the publish-note door — that stamps every note it files, registers it, and hashes it into the master list. But the building also has open windows: anyone on the team can climb in by writing the note page and editing the master list by hand, and the list is just a text file, so a careful climber leaves no trace. That is how we got thirty-two repair jobs: notes kept appearing in the library without ever going through the door, and other lanes kept cleaning up after them. This design does not add a thirty-third cleanup. It seals the windows. The door starts chaining every note it registers to the note before it, like pages sewn into a ledger — tear one out or sew one in by hand and the stitching breaks where everyone can see it. The checker learns to inspect the stitching every time. The landing gate makes the check mandatory instead of advisory. And the library's shelves — the reader, the feed, the brain index — only stock notes whose stitching verifies, so a note that sneaks in any other way simply does not exist for readers. Filing around the door stops being a shortcut and becomes a dead end.
intelligence.what_it_means: The scorecard (weights: closes the bypass 40 · does not block legitimate filing 15 · reversibility 10 · cost to build 15 · failure mode when the door is down 20). A) Receipt chain alone — 6.5: elegant and cheap, but with no gate it only detects; a determined lane can still land and surface. B) Required checks alone — 6.1: blocks the PR route, but the check is satisfiable by a self-complete filing in the same commit, direct landings by bypass actors still pass, and a broken door tool halts all filing everywhere. C) Registry as single-minter projection — 6.45: strong on registry edits, but bare pages still land, registration lags async, and path protection needs the same ruleset change anyway. D) Consumer fail-closed alone — 6.95: best manners, worst closure: a self-minted capture+entry passes every binding check and still surfaces, so the band keeps forming upstream. E) The composite (A+B+D, checker completed) — 7.5, the winner: each layer covers the layer above's hole — the chain makes forgery cost exactly as much as compliance, the completed checker makes forgery visible, the required gate makes a defective landing impossible for non-bypass identities, and the consumer backstop makes any residual landing worthless. The losers lost on the same fact from different sides: any single layer leaves one of the four proven routes open. E's honest ceiling: it cannot reach 9 while main requires no check and all seats share one identity — the design names both as external facts instead of pretending to engineer around them.
whats_inside: The four bypass routes found in code: direct push to main, self-complete filing in one commit, the NAYA-NOTES side door, and scoped deploy-key/App bypass of the pull_request ruleset rule

page.how_it_connects: It builds on the door as it exists: publish-note (tools/learning_loop.py, classic path in tools/smart_note_v2.py publish_classic) is the only writer this design blesses, and check_door_obligation.py is the checker it completes — including the CaptureIndex indexing gap that produced the SN-4203..4207 CONFLICT class on 2026-11-20. It applies SN-0111 (a seal proves consistency, not authorship) as a design constraint rather than discovering it afterward. It depends on the Hub reader's existing registry gating (HUB/hub-worker.js serveNote resolves slug → registry entry → projection_path) and names the one external dependency honestly: the required-check ruleset change is Shawn's settings gate, the same class as branch protection. It is the first item of the Option B program the Plan-to-60 re-audit adopted on 2026-11-22 (hole-closing outcomes first, cures demoted to housekeeping), and its graduation test is the one Clarity and Verity were assigned in the 2026-11-21 Fourteen Questions execution order.
page.machine: DESIGN SPEC — THE SEALED DOOR (build in this order; each step independently reversible). STEP 1 (writer stamp): in tools/smart_note_v2.py publish_classic(), inside the registry transaction in register_classic(), compute door_receipt = sha256(canon(capture_without_receipt) || page_hash || prev_content_hash) with prev = content_hash of the current last entries[] element (genesis: '0'*64); stamp published_via, door_version, door_receipt onto final_capture BEFORE the capture file is written (capture is written first in the sequence, so the stamp must be computed from a registry read that the transaction then re-verifies — if the registry moved between read and transaction, the transaction recomputes or refuses; never stamp against a stale manifest). Store door_receipt on the registry entry. STEP 2 (checker indexing): check_door_obligation.py CaptureIndex gains by_filename (capture path stem), by_top_ib (top-level intelligent_block_id), by_file (top-level file), and registry capture_file resolution; for_page() consults filename first. This kills the false NO_CAPTURE/CONFLICT class for every classic capture (root of SN-4203..4207). STEP 3 (checker completeness): NO_CAPTURE checked for every entry carrying capture_file, regardless of entry presence; corpus_manifest_hash recomputed and compared every run (mismatch = defect MANIFEST_STALE, exit 1); receipt chain verified over door-stamped entries in stored order (break = defect CHAIN_BROKEN with the first broken SN named); grandfather ratchet: entries registered before the chain start are listed in a checked-in ratchet file, and the ratchet may only shrink. STEP 4 (workflow shape): door-obligation.yml triggers on all pull_requests and pushes (delta mode; exits 0 immediately when the range touches no note paths), keeping fail-closed exit 2 on machinery errors; brain-index-freshness wired the same way. STEP 5 (ruleset — the design's ONE human gate, Shawn's settings change): add door-obligation and brain-index-freshness as required status checks on main; remove bypass actors for the note paths (BRAIN/05-MEMORY/**, .naya/capture/**, .naya/memory/**) so automated identities land note changes only through a green PR; the App keeps bypass elsewhere so feed/map lanes are untouched. STEP 6 (consumer backstop): regenerate_brain_index.py builds its corpus from pages that carry a verified registry entry (entry present, hashes bind, chain or ratchet or reconstruction marker valid); a bare page is reported as UNREGISTERED_PAGE and excluded, never absorbed; hub reader and feed are already registry-gated and need no change. STEP 7 (guardian teeth): post-merge-guardian gains auto-revert for the narrow door-defect class only (page landed on main with NO_ENTRY / CHAIN_BROKEN / MANIFEST_STALE), revert commit through the same Git Data API route, board alarm as today. GRADUATION TEST (P-152): red-team attempts, all four must fail to register AND fail to surface — (i) direct-push a bare IB page; (ii) self-complete single commit (page + hand-written capture + hand-edited registry, hashes correctly recomputed); (iii) forged receipt computed against a stale manifest; (iv) Git Data API landing of a forged trio. Then three consecutive production filing batches land with zero filed-but-unregistered band and zero cures. On pass: cure lane retires, P-152 graduates to law. FAILURE MODES BY DESIGN: door tooling broken → note filing halts on note paths only (fail-closed where it matters), captures can still be authored locally and published when the door returns; checker broken → exit 2 blocks note landings, nothing else; ruleset change is a toggle — full reversibility in one settings action. KNOWN LIMITS, stated plainly: the receipt chain is tamper-evidence, not authorship proof (SN-0111); an actor holding Shawn-level settings access is out of scope by definition; the NAYA-NOTES corpus awaits a scope ruling and is NOT inside this perimeter.
page.the_learning: Declared behavior change: from now on, enforcement is designed at the writer side and proven by red-team, never by cure count. A filing route that can be walked around will be walked around — thirty-two cures are the receipt — so the standard for any future obligation in this system is: the compliant path is the only path that produces a visible result, verification runs where the work happens, and detection without reversal is a cost center, not a control. When a design's ceiling is set by a fact outside the design (a settings gate, a shared identity), the design names the fact and its owner instead of claiming a score the evidence cannot carry.
page.what_is_in_it_for_you: For Shawn: the cure treadmill ends — no more parked bands, no more escalation posts about filing collisions, and the one decision this design needs from you is a single settings change, presented when the build is ready and proven, not before. For filing seats: nothing changes in your hands — you already file through publish-note; the door simply becomes the only way in instead of the recommended way. For readers: every note that opens is a note that was stamped, chained, and verified — the library's contents become trustworthy by construction. For the fleet: an entire recurring lane (band cures) is deleted from the workload forever, and its minutes go to hole-closing work.
page.why_it_matters: Every cure costs a lane-run, a landing, a verification, and a board receipt — thirty-two times for one unchanged cause, while the band regrows behind each cure (thirteen notes sit parked behind PR #3518 right now because even curing them would race another lane). Writer-side enforcement converts a recurring operational cost into a one-time build: after it, the filed-but-unregistered band cannot form, the cure lane's entire workload disappears, and every note a reader can open is a note the door stamped. It is also the graduation test of principle P-152 — the standing lesson that obligations must be enforced where the work happens, not inspected afterward.

title: The Sealed Door: Writer-Side Enforcement for Smart Note Filing
